- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later — suggest adjusting for mean reversion toward historical median.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and overreact — reduce forecast by 2–5% for such periods.
- Model underestimates when true price drops below 80 — apply upward bias correction for low-price regimes.
- Forecast lags true price by 1–3 days in most cases — adjust for 1-day lag in rolling forecasts.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the first 10 days — apply downward correction of 1–3% for early forecast days.
- When true price is below 80, model often fails to recognize the trend — add a “low-price buffer” to prevent underestimation.
